exempt.no-twin:GET /v1/mcp-servers/callback: ANSWERED 2026-09-16, and this one can never have a twin. It is the far side redirecting a BROWSER back after a person approved a sign-in, so it is the one unauthenticated route in its group by necessity: the browser carries no bearer of ours. Its gate is the single-use state, bound to the owner who started the round and consumed before the code is exchanged. An agent tool for it would be meaningless — the code is delivered by the redirect, the state dies on first use, and an agent holding both would be replaying somebody else's round. What an agent CAN do is start one: aimeat_mcp_authorize, which returns the address for a person to open and can approve nothing itself.

exempt.no-twin:POST /v1/mcp-servers/node: ANSWERED 2026-09-16, and the answer is that only a person may reach this one. It attaches a server to the WHOLE NODE, and the fields it reads say why: `token` is a credential somebody pastes, and `availability`, `allowlist` and `price` decide who on this node may spend it and what they are charged. The door stands behind requireOperatorPrincipal(), which admits the operator IN PERSON and refuses everything acting in their name, so an agent twin would either be dead on arrival or would be a way around that check. The policy half IS reachable by an agent, through aimeat_mcp_registry_set, and that tool now takes every policy field this door takes; what it cannot do is the first attachment, which is the act this exemption is about. An operator's own agent that wanted to attach one would ask the operator to do it, which is the intended answer rather than a gap.
exempt.no-twin:POST /v1/app-grants/authorize-co: ANSWERED 2026-09-19: only a person may reach this one. It is the owner approving the permissions an APP asks for; an agent that could press it could grant apps permissions in the owner's name, which is the one act consent exists to keep with the person. It surfaced on 2026-09-19 only because the decision provider's request schema (DecideRequest) made `state` a record-field name, and this door reads the OAuth `state` parameter; nothing about the door changed.
